evidence: PC9 intermittently loses access while another PC uses the same network.
R11 show arp output lists Internet address 192.168.100.10 bound to MAC address aaaa.bbbb.0001 on Gi0/0.
R11 show arp output lists Internet address 192.168.100.10 bound to MAC address cccc.dddd.0002 on Gi0/0.
root_cause: A duplicate IP address conflict exists for 192.168.100.10, which is bound to multiple MAC addresses (aaaa.bbbb.0001 and cccc.dddd.0002) on interface Gi0/0.
verification: Run show arp on R11 and confirm that IP address 192.168.100.10 maps to only a single unique MAC address.
Manually test PC9 connectivity to ensure intermittent loss of access is resolved.
fix_steps: Verify the duplicate ARP entries for IP address 192.168.100.10 on R11 interface Gi0/0.
Identify the conflicting devices associated with MAC addresses aaaa.bbbb.0001 and cccc.dddd.0002.
Reassign a unique IPv4 address to one of the conflicting network devices.
Clear the ARP cache on R11 to remove stale entries if necessary.
Test network connectivity and stability for PC9.

rule_checker_findings.evidence: IPv4 address 192.168.100.10 is bound to multiple MAC addresses / host interfaces in ARP data.
rule_checker_findings.recommended_action: Reassign a unique IPv4 address to one of the conflicting network devices.
